text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-Fourteen of Norways largest hospitals show a total deficit of 350 million crowns for 1996.

-Atle Skaardal took super-giant slalom gold to become the first Norwegian to win successive Alpine skiing world titles. And the day only got better for Norway when compatriot Lasse Kjus captured silver.

-Oil companies are losing interest in drilling for oil in the Barent Sea. It seems that several major companies will fail to apply for a stake in the Barents Sea initiative launched by the Norwegian Energy Ministry.
-A subsidiary of Norwegian shipbulider and construction group Kvaerner, Kvaerner Mandal, may be seeking to win contracts for 17 minesweepers in countries in the Middle East and the Far East.
-Sweden's plans to phase out nuclear plants opens up for Norwegian export of natural gas to the neighbouring country.
-Norway's state-owned telecommunication company Telenor needs 50 billion crowns for investments the next seven to eight years.
-Norwegian metal producer Elkem sees increased sales in Asia. At the outset Elkem will invest modestly in Asia, but it will consider expanding later on.
